buildings.purpose: Blocks a monster until the wall breaks, so the bite never reaches the keep.
Shoots the nearest monster and spends wood and gold to cover a side the heroes are not on.
Bursts for a large hit when a monster steps on it, then it is gone.
Feeds the stockpile with food and a little gold during the day.
Raises every attack's damage while the building stands.
Raises mage damage and shortens mage cooldowns while the spire stands.

edges.via: Any living hero who stands on a tree chops wood.
Placing a wall pays its wood cost.
A tower costs wood and gold.
A trap costs wood.
A field costs wood. A farmer pays less.
The forge costs wood and gold.
The spire costs wood and gold.
A barricade pays wood and lays three walls.
A tower costs gold as well as wood.
The forge costs gold as well as wood.
The spire costs gold as well as wood.
Sow places a field without paying wood.
Fields yield food during the build, and a living farmer doubles that yield.
Fields also add a little gold during the build.
Harvest collects food from nearby fields.
Feeding beside the keep spends food and restores keep health.
Feast spends food and heals every living hero.
A kill pays the monster's bounty. A warrior kill pays one extra gold.
An engineer pays less wood for walls, towers, and traps, and can raise a line of walls.
The engineer's swing repairs the nearest building.
A monster that cannot walk through a wall bites the wall instead of the keep.
A standing tower fires arrows at a monster in range.
A trap damages the monster that steps on it.
Strike, dash, and nova damage monsters in front of the warrior.
Guard cuts the damage of bites against that hero.
Bolt, fireball, and meteor damage monsters. Frost slows them.
Mark makes a monster take more damage. Volley and the shot damage it.
A living scout reveals the next wave's directions before the last five seconds.
A standing forge multiplies attack damage for every hero.
A standing spire raises mage damage and shortens mage cooldowns.
A monster in reach of the keep bites it. A boss slam hits harder.
A monster that is closer to a hero than to the keep bites the hero.
Killing a boss adds one relic the party does not already hold.
Heartwood raises the keep's maximum health.
Whetstone adds damage and swiftness adds move speed.
Granary adds extra food to the field yield.
CONCEPT.md says elites drop relics too. Only a boss drops one today.
CONCEPT.md describes a mage tower that unlocks spell upgrades. The spire only buffs damage and cooldown.
CONCEPT.md describes the settlement growing into a walled city. Players place buildings by hand. There is no city-growth layer.
Monster bodies do not block each other, so a wall line cannot squeeze them into a gap.
Heroes do not block monsters. The planned rule is that bodies block, and the warrior dash is the one pass through a monster.
Heroes do not block other heroes.
The keep is not solid. slide has the flag, and every caller passes false.
Monsters can walk into the keep and bite it from inside. They should attack from the edge.
A keep upgrade that spends wood and gold is not built. There is no card pick.
An upgrade should widen the build radius and pull the camera back. The radius is still the hero kit range.
The client draws a tree ring that is not an entity and has no wood. Real trees are chopped until they disappear.
